manifest: ICPSR 39331 (Pukelis) — SNAP COVID-19 Policy & Enrollment data: structure, provenance, and the public download path
status_reason: The assembled panel is redistributed only via ICPSR (free account + click-through terms) and Dropbox (raw). Neither is fetchable non-interactively, and the ICPSR download is a gated public-use file we do not bypass. This manifest vendors the public structure + provenance + the exact manual download path; tools/snap-enrollment-panel/ turns the downloaded delimited files into CA artifacts with one command.

study.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program COVID-19 Policy and Enrollment Data, United States, 1987-2024
study.author: Pukelis, Kelsey
study.companion_paper: Pukelis, K. — 'SNAP Policies and Enrollment following the COVID-19 Pandemic' (http://kelseypukelis.com/files/Pukelis_SNAPcovid.pdf)
study.access: Public-use, no restriction type. FREE ICPSR account required to download (Create Account -> agree to terms -> Download -> Delimited). NOT embargoed, NOT restricted-use. We do not bypass the login.
study.license_note: Public-use research data via ICPSR terms of use; underlying enrollment numbers are public state-agency records and the COVID-policy facts are public USDA FNS records.

build_code.what_it_holds: Code to import, clean, and combine the SNAP state- and county-level enrollment files; plus snap_data_availability.csv listing the ORIGINAL public state-agency source URLs for each state's raw enrollment files.
build_code.availability_csv: snap_data_availability.csv — per-state source links to the original public agency files (the raw inputs the build code assembles).
build_code.raw_data_mirror: Dropbox (linked from the repo) holds the raw downloaded inputs; the final combined+documented data is the ICPSR deposit.

datasets.name: SNAP COVID Policy Data
datasets.geography: all 50 states + DC (+ territories Guam, USVI)
key_fields: number of months certification periods were extended

instruments.emergency_allotment: Supplemental benefits raising every household to (initially) the max allotment, then (post-Apr-2021) a +$95 floor. Families First Coronavirus Response Act (PL 116-127, 2020-03-18); ENDED nationally after Feb 2023 benefits (Consolidated Appropriations Act 2023).
instruments.recert_waiver: Temporary waiver / extension of recertification and periodic-report (interview) requirements; cert periods extended by N months.
instruments.simplified_application: Waived or adjusted application / interview steps to simplify enrollment during the PHE.

datasets.primary_public_source: USDA FNS COVID-19 waivers pages (https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/waivers, .../disaster/pandemic/covid-19, .../snap/expiration-program-flexibilities-covid-19), backfilled via the Internet Archive Wayback Machine.

datasets.name: SNAP County Enrollment Data
datasets.geography: counties with state + county FIPS (territories excluded); a LIMITED subset of states (not all 50) for the demographic breakdowns
datasets.role: DEPENDENT VARIABLE (DV) — county-month enrollment level + month-over-month change (the churn/retention signal)
key_fields: county name, state name + abbr, state FIPS, county FIPS
households, individuals, adults, children, infants, elderly, disabled enrolled in SNAP
(for some states) total benefits issued, applications, recertifications, plus a few TANF + Medicaid measures
datasets.primary_public_source: Individual state-agency SNAP websites (per snap_data_availability.csv). For California the equivalent public series is CDSS DFA256 'Food Stamp Program Participation and Benefit Issuance Report' on data.chhs.ca.gov.
datasets.ca_caveat: California's inclusion/completeness in DS2 is NOT guaranteed — DS2 covers a limited set of states. Confirm CA presence after download; if absent, the CDSS DFA256 county series is the public CA fallback (see README).

datasets.name: SNAP State Enrollment Detail Data
datasets.role: context — long state-month enrollment series (+ for some states gender/race/ethnicity breakdowns)
datasets.primary_public_source: USDA FNS SNAP Data Tables / State Activity Reports + state agencies.

civica_use.regression_role: DS2 = the churn/retention dependent variable at county-month (enrollment level + ΔMoM); DS1 = clean COVID-waiver instruments (EA on/off, recert-waiver on/off, simplified-application on/off, cert-extension-months). The recert-waiver and EA on/off transitions (esp. the Mar-2023 EA cliff) are the strongest exogenous shocks for identifying how renewal/recert friction moves enrollment — directly Civica's retention pillar.
complements: cdss-cf18 (CA procedural churn at the recert/SAR-7 moment — mechanism)
usda-qc-ca + caper (error on the application/denial side)
civica_use.why_highest_value: It is the only true LONGITUDINAL county-month enrollment PANEL in the stack (1993-2024) and the only one with built-in policy IVs — everything else here is cross-sectional or a single state series. It is the missing panel a difference-in-differences / event-study retention model needs.

download_path_manual: 1. Create a FREE ICPSR account: https://www.icpsr.umich.edu (Create Account; Google/ORCID/institutional email all work).

3. Download tab -> agree to the Terms of Use -> choose 'Delimited' format. You get a zip per dataset (DS0001 = COVID policy, DS0002 = county enrollment, DS0003 = state detail) with a .tsv/.txt data file + codebook.
4. Run tools/snap-enrollment-panel/src/ingest_snap_panel.py --ds2 DS0002...tsv --ds1 DS0001...tsv --state CA to emit the CA county-month panel + CA COVID-policy state-month table into this directory.

(Alternative, fully no-login but more work: clone https://github.com/kpukelis/snap_data, read snap_data_availability.csv, and re-pull the per-state-agency raw files it links — then run the repo's build code.)
what_is_vendored_here: Only this manifest (public structure + provenance + IV/DV definitions + the exact download path) and PROVENANCE.md. The bulk county-month rows are NOT vendored because they are only redistributed through the gated ICPSR/Dropbox deposit; they materialize locally once the operator runs the one-time download + the ingest script above.
